Mon 16 Monday Nov 16 Tue 17 Tuesday Nov 17 Wed 18 Wednesday Nov 18 Thu 19 Thursday Nov 19 Fri 20 Friday Nov 20 Filters Filters Learning Level ( learn more ) Beginner Intermediate Advanced Topics Observability & SRE Security Architecture AI & ML DevEx & Frontends Modern Languages & Infrastructure Platform Engineering Teams & Orgs Clear filters Apply Beginner For those learning about a topic for the first time or looking to gain foundational knowledge before starting a project. For these presentations, you will walk away with a conceptual understanding, knowledge of basic tools, and/or the first steps required to try it out. Intermediate Sessions for those actively working with the technology daily and who want to improve their efficiency, testing, and/or application of best practices. In these sessions, you may learn concrete code examples, testing strategies, common pitfalls, and/or methods to solve medium-complexity problems. Advanced For the attendees who are actively designing or leading projects with a particular technology and want to understand complex trade-offs, scalability, and integration challenges. These sessions may allow you to gain unique, production-tested insights, architectural patterns, performance optimization tips, and/or analysis of design trade-offs. Resharding under heavy load is notoriously difficult. How do you move gigabytes of state across live database nodes without dropping keys, blocking the main event loop, or breaking client abstractions? Jacob Murphy - Google Ballroom BC Advanced Topic Track: Guardrails & Safety Nets (Evals) for the New Landscape Token Efficiency at Uber Details coming soon. Ballroom A Track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents APIs That Can't Afford to Be Wrong: Lessons from Moving Money Most API design advice assumes a forgiving environment: retries are cheap, data has a single source of truth, and a slow response is only an inconvenience. Financial infrastructure assumes none of that. Card networks give you three seconds to auth or decline. Fawziyah Alebiosu - Imprint Pacific DEKJ Track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time The Freeze Paradox: Why Stopping Deployments Doesn't Stop Failures When systems fail at Netflix and in an environment this complex, they sometimes will, the instinctive response is to freeze deployments. Prachi Jain - Netflix Sandhya Narayan - Netflix Seacliff ABC Intermediate Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track I Legacy vs. AI-Native Is the Wrong Question: Architecting the Modern Platform Engineering leaders modernizing operational platforms are often presented with a false binary: choose the control and reliability of established enterprise platforms or embrace AI-native tools optimized for speed, automation, and intelligent experiences. Payal Patel - Freshworks Saiprasad Murali - Freshworks Pacific LM No Video Available Intermediate Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track II Model-Harness Co-Training: Data-Driven Optimization Toward Pareto-Optimal Agents Teams with agents in production are chasing the optimal agent. Usually they pick one lever: tune the harness (the prompts, tools, memory, and workflow around the model), or fine-tune the model, but the two depend on each other. Ballroom BC Track: Guardrails & Safety Nets (Evals) for the New Landscape How Airbnb Guardrailed Its AI Customer Support Agent When Airbnb launched its AI customer support assistant, the feature made the news — the guardrails built to make it safe to ship did not. Yet an AI agent that talks to millions of customers, remembers a conversation across turns, and can trigger account actions is a Weiping Peng - Airbnb Ballroom A No Video Available Track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents Everything I Knew About Developer Experience Is Wrong for Agents Most of what we know about developer experience we learned from humans. Agents are a different user, and some of our best practices quietly work against them. Emmanuel Paraskakis - Level 250 Pacific DEKJ Track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time Adapt or Drift: Resilience Engineering When AI Moves the Operating Point Resilient systems do not stay resilient by standing still. They survive by adapting. But adaptation comes with risk: under sustained pressure, organizations and systems can slowly drift toward failure while still appearing to operate normally. Women & Allies in Tech Lunch Session in Waterfront AB, Atrium level (registration required). 01:35PM PST Track: Architectures You've Always Wondered About How to Build a Real-Time Voice Agent A voice agent looks like a chatbot with a microphone. Rishabh Bhargava Ballroom BC Intermediate Topic Track: Guardrails & Safety Nets (Evals) for the New Landscape LLM Flip-Flops: From Reliability Risk to a Hill-Climbing Signal Run the same task through the same LLM twice, and you may get two materially different answers. This behavior is often dismissed as the stochastic nature of LLMs, but it creates a serious product risk. Dianhuan Lin - Datadog Ballroom A Track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents The Schema Was Never Enough: The World in Protocols Every reliable process in the world is a protocol: auctions, double-entry bookkeeping, brokerage account transfers, or APIs. Protocols reduce ambiguity but the world remains messy. Ryan Scott Brown - Crunchyroll Pacific DEKJ Intermediate Topic Track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time Unconference: Resilience Engineering Seacliff D No Video Available Track: Sponsored Solution Track I Your Agents Lack Context: Here's How to Fix 'You're absolutely right!"' Every AI coding tool can generate code. Very few can generate the right code for your organization, because they’re missing context. Brandon Waselnuk - UNBLOCKED Pacific LM Intermediate Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track II Sponsored session Details coming soon! Marina 02:25PM PST Break 02:45PM PST Track: Architectures You've Always Wondered About Inside the Disaggregated Architecture Serving LLM Inference Every LLM request is really two very different jobs. Reading your prompt (prefill) is compute-intensive, while generating the response token by token (decode) is dominated by memory bandwidth. For years, the industry ran both phases on the same hardware and accepted the compromise. Nancy Zheng - Cerebras Ballroom BC Interview Available Track: Guardrails & Safety Nets (Evals) for the New Landscape Unconference: Guardrails & Safety Nets Seacliff D No Video Available Track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents No New Backend: The API Layer Behind 800+ Agent-Built Apps at Duolingo At Duolingo, anyone (engineer or not) can describe an internal tool and get a working app back, deployed against real company systems. That's BuildingHub, and 350 Duolingo employees have created at least one app with it. Sarah Deitke - Duolingo Pacific DEKJ Intermediate Topic Track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time Saturation: How Your Software Will Fail at Scale Even in the ethereal world of software, everything has a limit. And, once that limit is reached, very bad things can happen. In this talk, we will explore the problem of saturation: when a software system runs into one of these limits. Lorin Hochstein - Airbnb Seacliff ABC Interview Available Intermediate Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track I Wait, You're Still Doing PRs? PRs were built for open source. A non-maintainer wanted to contribute, a maintainer needed a gate, and you opened the PR early so the two of you could work through the change together while it was still forming. That was the point. The PR was where the thinking happened. Lee Faus - Atomic Pacific LM No Video Available Intermediate Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track II The Context Gap: Why Correct Agents Fail Two agents edit different files. Git merges clean. The program is broken. No conflict was thrown, because the collision was in meaning, not in text — and business decisions are almost all semantic. Xiaowei Jiang - Tacnode Inc. Is your incident severity a complex word problem? Do you arbitrate which severity an incident should be during the incident itself? Do you know what the difference between your severities are? Do you even have incident severity in your org? Em Ruppe - Chime Seacliff ABC Beginner Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track I AI Amplifies Everything, Including Your Mess: Lessons from Delivering with AI at Global Scale AI doesn’t fix how a team works. It multiplies it. This talk shares real lessons from an engineering team rebuilding its software development lifecycle around AI while delivering Nu Global, a product that scales financial services globally on top of crypto rails. Caio Sousa - NU Pacific LM No Video Available Track: Sponsored Solution Track II Sponsored Session Details coming soon! Marina No Video Available 04:45PM PST Break 05:05PM PST Track: Architectures You've Always Wondered About Unconference: Architectures You've Always Wondered About Seacliff D No Video Available Track: Guardrails & Safety Nets (Evals) for the New Landscape Testing & Verification for Code-Generating Agents Details coming soon. Ballroom A Track: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents Stop Fighting the Remodel: API Design for Models That Outgrew Their Boundaries Every domain model has a breaking point. At Netflix, ours arrived all at once—Ads, Games, Live events, and entirely new kinds of content. Each pulled the core entities in different, sometimes contradictory directions. Aarti Gupta - Netflix Pacific DEKJ Intermediate Topic Track: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time It's Never the Thing That Broke: Learning From Incidents at (AI) Speed When something breaks, our first instinct is to focus on the thing that failed. But in complex systems, the failure is usually the result of many things going right, changing, and interacting in ways we didn't anticipate. Vanessa Huerta Granda - Enova Seacliff ABC Track: Sponsored Solution Track I Apache Spark: Structured Streaming Real-Time Mode Apache Spark Structured Streaming is a distributed stream processing engine built on Spark SQL and is widely used for ETL-style workloads, where seconds- to minutes-level latency is acceptable. But millisecond-latency use cases have historically been out of reach. Jerry Peng - Databricks Pacific LM No Video Available Track: Sponsored Solution Track II Sponsored session Details coming soon! Marina No Video Available 06:00PM PST Conference Social - Dry Snacks & Drinks - Ballroom Foyer & Pacific Level - Ends at 7pm Tuesday, November 17th, 2026 08:00AM PST Continental Breakfast - Pacific Level 09:00AM PST Conference Introduction and Keynote: Learning Out Loud (Under Near-Existential Pressure) Laura Savino - Adobe Photoshop 10:10AM PST Break Tracks Distributed Systems in Production Vidhya Arvind - Netflix Engineering AI Systems Melanie Zhao - BlackRock Staff+ Engineering Skills Javier Fernandez-Ivern - Netflix Data Platforms Reimagined Adi Polak - Confluent Sponsored Solution Track III 10:35AM PST Track: Distributed Systems in Production Orderly Keys, Wild Values: Adaptive Compression for Distributed Key-Value Storage At Netflix scale - billions of requests per day and petabytes of key-value data - even small inefficiencies in storage and network paths become expensive. Joseph Lynch - Netflix Ayushi Singh - Netflix Ballroom BC Intermediate Topic Track: Engineering AI Systems Skills, Memory, or Fine-Tuning? The Engineering Loop Behind Self-Improving Agents As agents become mainstream, everyone wants to improve theirs either by making fewer mistakes on existing tasks or by taking on harder ones. This usually happens once an agent is already deployed in production. Abhinav Sinha - Lucidic AI Ballroom A Advanced Topic Track: Staff+ Engineering Skills Nobody Knows Everything (and That's OK): Building Alignment in Complex, Rapidly Changing Environments Successful Staff+ engineers build alignment across organizational and technical boundaries, including domains where they aren't the deepest expert. Kaye Mason - Meta Pacific DEKJ Advanced Topic Track: Data Platforms Reimagined Breaking Down the Walls to Python & Big Data + AI Performance with Transpilation and LLMs Many of us have a love hate relationship with Apache Spark, especially when it comes to PySpark. Especially in Python, the UDF performance can be a dumpster fire. Holden Karau - Snowflake Seacliff ABC Intermediate Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track III Feeling Faster Isn’t a Metric: Measuring AI’s Real Engineering Impact AI adoption in engineering is settled. In GitKraken’s 2026 State of AI in Engineering survey of 554 developers and engineering leaders, 96% of teams had adopted AI coding tools and 84% of developers said they feel more productive. Only about one in five can actually measure the impact. Jeremy Castile - GitKraken Pacific L-O No Video Available 11:25AM PST Break 11:45AM PST Track: Distributed Systems in Production How to Build Online Systems with Object Storage “Diskless” systems that delegate durability to object storage are everywhere, and for three good reasons: Almog Gavra - responsive.dev Ballroom BC Intermediate Topic Track: Engineering AI Systems Inside Asimov: BlackRock’s Platform Architecture for Applied AI at Scale BlackRock’s Portfolio Management Group is transforming how investment teams conduct research by combining deep investment expertise with shared AI capabilities. Dan Wolf - BlackRock Sri Annapurna Bhupatiraju - BlackRock Ballroom A Track: Staff+ Engineering Skills Use AI to Multiply Your Team as a Staff Engineer Most "AI for engineers" content is about typing faster. That's IC-level work. Staff engineers have a different question to answer. When AI raises the floor on what every engineer can ship, what is the staff engineer's job, and where does the leverage actually come from now? Jordan Cutler - Pinterest Pacific DEKJ Intermediate Topic Track: Data Platforms Reimagined Building a Data Platform with AI Data platform sits at the intersection of infrastructure, governance, operations, and user experience. Mouli Mukherjee - OpenAI Seacliff ABC Beginner Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track III Notes From 300 Installs Inside Someone Else's Cloud We run our storage and query backend inside our customers' own VPCs. They own the infrastructure. We own the pager. I'm the person who helps installs it, so I've watched this architecture meet a few hundred different production Kubernetes environments and I've kept notes on what went wrong. Adam Hicks - Groundcover Pacific LM No Video Available 12:35PM PST Lunch ( menus ) & Lunch topic discussions on Atrium level. 01:35PM PST Track: Distributed Systems in Production Autoscaling 800 Valkey Clusters: Distributed Systems Lessons from Scaling Stateful Fleets Autoscaling stateless services is a solved problem. In a sharded datastore, a resize is not a capacity change — it's moving ownership of key ranges between nodes while the cluster serves live traffic, and rebalancing takes long enough that reacting to a traffic peak is already too late. Kishor Yadav Kommanaboina - Snap Inc Ballroom BC Track: Engineering AI Systems The Revenge of the Data Scientist: Why Reliable AI Needs Evals, Traces, and Metrics Most teams can now ship an AI prototype by calling a foundation-model API. The hard part is knowing whether that system works when real users, messy data, and business consequences arrive. Hamel Husain Ballroom A Intermediate Topic Track: Staff+ Engineering Skills Scaling Tech by Aligning Humans Scaling a complex technology can get messy without a clear north star or a shared technical strategy. Product strategies from different functions can each deliver impact but may lead to disconnected solutions or inadvertently introduce various forms of technical debt. Scott Behrens - Netflix Pacific DEKJ Intermediate Topic Track: Data Platforms Reimagined One Does Not Simply Add Synchronous Writes - Bridging Batch and Real Time with Apache Iceberg What happens when a batch ingestion platform needs to behave like an operational database? Datadog’s Reference Tables product was designed for asynchronous uploads of large datasets, but customers increasingly needed synchronous row-level edits, without sacrificing batch scale. Paige Elinson - Datadog Seacliff ABC Track: Sponsored Solution Track III Why Your Document AI Fails in Production — And How to Fix the Infrastructure Underneath It The session explains why document AI that works in demos can fail in production: document structure can be lost during ingestion, rendering can break on edge cases, and extraction can vary across runs. When agents make routing or approval decisions, teams also need governance. Pavitter Josan - Nutrient Pacific LM No Video Available Intermediate Topic 02:25PM PST Break 02:45PM PST Track: Distributed Systems in Production Unconference: Distributed Systems in Production Seacliff D No Video Available Track: Engineering AI Systems Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI Engineering is shifting from synchronous, line-by-line implementation to an asynchronous model in which agents execute, verify, and retry while humans own intent, architecture, constraints, and release decisions.  Brian Yang - OpenAI Ballroom A Intermediate Topic Track: Staff+ Engineering Skills Transitioning From a Startup to a Mature Platform What you need to succeed in a startup with zero customers is different from what you need when you have a few thousand, and this changes many times as the company grows. Some of these changes are code and architectural changes, some are organizational changes, and some are mindset shifts. Joy Ebertz - Imprint Ballroom BC Intermediate Topic Track: Data Platforms Reimagined Building a StreamHouse: Turning Kafka Streams into a Millisecond Query Layer AI agents have compressed business decisions from minutes to seconds. Data systems need to keep up. Seacliff ABC Track: Sponsored Solution Track III Trust, but Verify: Delivering Quality with Agentic Workflows In spite of all the recent panic, nothing has really changed about software development. We’re worried about agents being unreliable. Newsflash: human devs are too. We’re worried about agents producing more code than we can read, but did you ever really do all your reviews within 24 hours? Adrian Hatch - Antithesis Pacific LM No Video Available Intermediate Topic 03:35PM PST Coffee Break & Snacks - Pacific Level 03:55PM PST Track: Distributed Systems in Production When Your Users Are Agents: Lessons from a Distributed Postgres Platform Distributed systems are built around assumptions about workload behavior: connections have reasonable lifetimes, retries eventually stop, traffic spikes have recognizable causes, and application code produces somewhat predictable query patterns. Gwen Shapira - Nile Platform Inc Ballroom BC Beginner Topic Track: Engineering AI Systems Bridging Retrieval and Ranking: From LLM Embeddings and Graph Features to a GPU-Served DLRM The LinkedIn Feed retrieval layer selects, within 120 ms, the handful of posts each member sees from hundreds of millions of candidates. This split-second decision shapes what over a billion professionals read and engage with every day. Sudarshan Srinivasa Ramanujam - LinkedIn Ballroom A Track: Staff+ Engineering Skills Learning What’s Already There: A Breadth-Based Approach To Onboarding When onboarding to a new organization, it's vital to bootstrap your network and context quickly. Laura de Vesine Pacific DEKJ Beginner Topic Track: Data Platforms Reimagined From Datasets to Data Products: Powering Trusted AI for Social Impact When an AI agent acts on a nonprofit's behalf, it's only as trustworthy as the data underneath it. At Blackbaud, we build software for the social impact sector, and nonprofits have relied on our data for decades. Shannon McKenzie - Blackbaud Seacliff ABC Intermediate Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track III Your Agents Have Amnesia: Lessons from Building a Memory Layer for Multi-Agent Systems Multi-agent systems have a data problem nobody warns you about. Agent B sees Agent A's final output and nothing else; the reasoning, the dead ends, and whatever Agent A figured out three steps in all get thrown away. Heather Downing - YugabyteDB Pacific LM No Video Available Intermediate Topic 04:45PM PST Break 05:05PM PST Track: Distributed Systems in Production Adaptive Systems in Production: What Recommendation Systems Can Teach Us About Agents As organizations race to build AI agents, many teams are encountering challenges that feel new: evaluation uncertainty, feedback loops, behavioral drift, exploration versus exploitation, and maintaining user trust in systems that continuously adapt.But these challenges are not new. Mallika Rao - Zocdoc Ballroom BC Track: Engineering AI Systems Failing in Layers: Lessons from Rebuilding Netflix's ML Serving Platform Everyone talks about model quality. Fewer people talk about what happens when that model has to serve real traffic without falling over, or why the system ended up shaped the way it did in the first place. Rajat Shah - Netflix Wenbing Bai - Netflix Ballroom A Track: Staff+ Engineering Skills Unconference: Staff+ Engineering Skills Seacliff D No Video Available Track: Data Platforms Reimagined Iceberg V4: The Next Chapter in Table Formats Apache Iceberg V3 adoption is growing and the community is already shaping what comes next. This talk walks through the emerging scope and priorities for the V4 table spec and progress of the proposals currently underway. Daniel Weeks - Databricks Seacliff ABC Intermediate Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track III Sponsored Session Details coming soon! Pacific LM No Video Available 06:00PM PST Reception - Dry Snacks & Drinks - Ballroom Foyer & Pacific Level - Ends at 6:30pm Wednesday, November 18th, 2026 08:00AM PST Continental Breakfast - Pacific Level 09:00AM PST Conference Introduction and Keynote: The Execution Muscle: Why Great Teams Are Built, Not Hired Charlotte de Jong Schouwenburg - Bravely 10:10AM PST Break Tracks Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop Julie Amundson - Google Engineering the Developer Experience Ankit Jain - Aviator Real World Platform Engineering Daniel Bryant - Syntasso Code Beyond Engineers & Engineering Teams Suhail Patel - Monzo Sponsored Solution Track IV 10:35AM PST Track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop How Netflix Retrofitted Its SDLC for AI Coding Agents Agentic tools amplify what’s already in the codebase. The agent works through your code, your architecture decisions, and the documentation around them. It follows what it can read and guesses at the rest. Mark Khuzam - Netflix Ballroom BC Intermediate Topic Track: Engineering the Developer Experience Features vs Futures Details coming soon. Kent Beck Ballroom A Track: Real World Platform Engineering Platform Engineering’s Second Act: From Vending Machine to Passport Control Three years ago on the QCon SF stage, I made the case for “Acceleration, Autonomy, and Accountability” as the pillars of a successful platform. Those pillars haven't moved. AI has just rewritten what each one requires, and the platform team's job along with it. Smruti Patel - Apollo Graph Alex Mann - Apollo Graph Pacific DEKJ Intermediate Topic Track: Code Beyond Engineers & Engineering Teams Builder-Driven Development: Rebuilding the Organization Around the Builder Most teams still run agent development the way they run traditional software projects. Requirements are written up front, builders execute against them, and a demo closes out the cycle. That model works poorly for agents, because the most useful information rarely comes from a planning document. Jyothi Nookula Seacliff ABC Track: Sponsored Solution Track IV Simulating the Universe, 100 Times Over: Engineering Highly- Concurrent Agent Testing Testing AI agents properly is surprisingly hard. Production data sources are moving targets, static datasets go stale, and pointing agents at real systems is risky and impossible to reproduce. Pacific LM No Video Available 11:25AM PST Break 11:45AM PST Track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop Making Production Legible to Agents: Lessons From Building an Observability MCP An agent that can query production telemetry can test its own hypotheses against reality, rather than hallucinate fictions. Observability tooling allows our agents to close the loop and benefit from production wisdom. Liz Fong-Jones - Honeycomb.io Ballroom BC Track: Engineering the Developer Experience No More Small Systems, How AI May Bring Large System Problems to Everyone Once you figure out how to use AI to make your organization productive, you will soon find you have a whole new set of problems. While some of those problems will be novel thanks to LLMs, many of them are just the result of there being "more stuff". Adam Bender - Google Ballroom A Interview Available Intermediate Topic Track: Real World Platform Engineering Beyond the Kubernetes API: Building LinkedIn’s Compute Platform LinkedIn’s Kubernetes-based compute platform spans more than 500k bare-metal machines, 5M pods, with thousands of developers doing more than 110k deploys a week. We don’t expose raw Kubernetes to developers and instead, provide a curated set of platform offerings. Ronak Nathani - LinkedIn Pacific DEKJ Beginner Topic Track: Code Beyond Engineers & Engineering Teams Legacy as Leverage: How Brownfield Work Builds Technical Judgment Legacy systems are often treated as a necessary evil: work to be endured before moving on to more “real, strategic” projects. Shine Garg - Uncharted Path Breakthroughs Seacliff ABC Advanced Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track IV The Men in Black Know What's in Your JavaScript and How to Fix it! Ever wonder what’s lurking in the dark corners of your node_modules, like unidentified flying dependencies sneaking aboard your project? In an age of escalating software supply chain attacks, knowing exactly what you're shipping is as vital as tracking strange lights in the sky. Chris DeMars - TuxCare Pacific LM No Video Available 12:35PM PST Lunch ( menus ) & Lunch topic discussions on Atrium level. 01:35PM PST Track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop Efficient GPU Agents: Infra for Autonomous LLM Perf Optimization Parasail serves open-weight LLMs on distributed clusters of GPUs managed by Kubernetes. The typical performance optimization loop is to reproduce a problem or measure a regression, iterate on code or config, set up and run benchmarks, and decide whether the change is worth shipping. Ben Segal - Parasail Ballroom BC Track: Engineering the Developer Experience Growing Engineers in the Era of Agentic Coding Early-career engineers are learning the craft in an environment where the surface they touch is often an agent, not a codebase. The instinct is to treat this as a rupture in how engineers grow. It isn't. Adam Berry - Netflix Ballroom A Track: Real World Platform Engineering Observability: The Missing Control Plane for Agentic Engineering As AI agents move from generating code to testing, deploying, and operating it, the important question is no longer “How autonomous is the agent?” It’s “What can this agent safely decide without a human?” Rachael Wonnacott Pacific DEKJ Track: Code Beyond Engineers & Engineering Teams The Death of the Code Review Code review was built for a world where humans wrote all the code. Laurie Voss - Arize AI Seacliff ABC Interview Available Beginner Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track IV Sponsored session Details coming soon! Pacific LM No Video Available 02:25PM PST Break 02:45PM PST Track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop Dreams on Paper: How Agents Learn from Experience Agents produce high-fidelity traces of everything they do. But traces alone don't produce memory. This talk introduces three primitives for turning session history into something actionable: Brian Douglas - Paper Compute Co. Ballroom BC Track: Engineering the Developer Experience Shipping Faster, Understanding Less AI is changing software development faster than our engineering practices are evolving, and yet many teams are facing growing pressure to ship features faster. But moving faster can create three related threats to software health: technical debt, cognitive debt, and intent debt. Margaret-Anne Storey - University of Victoria Ballroom A Beginner Topic Track: Real World Platform Engineering Why Most Platform Teams Fail: The Adoption Problem Nobody Wants to Own We have all seen the moment: the platform goes live, the launch deck looks sharp, the portal is polished, the golden paths are documented, and yet teams quietly continue doing things the old way. Not always because the platform is bad, but because adoption was assumed, not owned. Shweta Vohra - Booking.com Pacific DEKJ Track: Code Beyond Engineers & Engineering Teams You Can't Read the Code Anymore - Verifying Software in the Age of AI AI writes most of the code now, so the hard part of engineering has moved from authoring to the part we’re worse at - verifying. With the incentives all pushing toward shipping faster and faster - the rational move is to skim the diff, click through a little manual QA, and ship on vibes. Omer van Kloeten - Forter Seacliff ABC Intermediate Topic Track: Sponsored Solution Track IV Sponsored session Details coming soon! Pacific LM No Video Available 03:35PM PST Coffee Break & Snacks - Pacific Level 03:55PM PST Track: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop Avoiding Prompt Debt & Other Context Failures As agents evolve, prompts get unruly. Edge cases are patched with one-line hotfixes, or with stacked instructions of escalating severity when an issue proves stubborn. Over time, those instructions pile up into a brittle artifact, overfit to an aging model. Drew Breunig - CMPND Ballroom BC Beginner Topic Track: Engineering the Developer Experience The Diary of an AI Adopter: How I Went From Skeptical to Enthusiastic in Our Organization’s AI Migration Efforts From market research reporting questionable success of AI adoption in enterprise, to CEOs announcing layoffs due to AI, to companies announcing they’re cutting back or eliminating AI due to prohibitive costs or technical missteps, it can be hard to know what the path to success should look like. Tara Hernandez - MongoDB Ballroom A Advanced Topic Track: Real World Platform Engineering Building a Migration Platform: Moving 100+ Netflix RDBMS Workloads to Aurora PostgreSQL In late 2024, Netflix made a bet: consolidate the vast majority of our relational database use cases onto a single engine: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Ammar Khaku - Netflix Kshitij Gupta - Netflix Pacific DEKJ Intermediate Topic Track: Code Beyond Engineers & Engineering Teams When Everyone Can Code, Who Owns Production? AI is making it dramatically easier to create and change software, but writing code is only one part of the software lifecycle. Every change still needs to be deployed, observed, operated, diagnosed, and kept reliable in production.
